value.explanation: 酉 is a wine jar used for fermentation.
孝 serves as a sound clue in an older form; its Japanese readings may differ.
One reading of the older form links 羊 with goodness.
力 means strength and contributes that meaning to 勝.
心 represents the heart and contributes meaning to 愛, love or affection.
日 represents the sun or a day. It contributes meaning to 時, time.
日 represents the sun in 晴, clear weather.
言 represents speech and words in 語, language.
氵 is the water component in 海, sea.
言 supplies the meaning of speech or words.
The 月-shaped part in 腕 represents 肉, flesh. Here it relates to the body, not the moon.
The 月-shaped part in 腹 represents 肉, flesh. Here it relates to the body, not the moon.
The 月-shaped part in 肺 represents 肉, flesh. Here it relates to the body, not the moon.
The 月-shaped part in 肌 represents 肉, flesh. Here it relates to the body, not the moon.
卜 pictures a crack used in fortune-telling.
言 contributes the meaning of speech or words in 討.
𠩺 supplies a historical sound component in 釐. Its meaning contribution is disputed.
The left side is the flesh component 肉 in its 月-shaped form. It marks 腺, a gland, as a body part.
腺 was coined in Japan with 泉 supplying the reading セン.
峡 uses the 夹-shaped component corresponding to 夾 as a historical sound clue; Japanese readings can differ.
挟 uses the 夹-shaped component corresponding to 夾 as a historical sound clue; Japanese readings can differ.
狭 uses the 夹-shaped component corresponding to 夾 as a historical sound clue; Japanese readings can differ.
夾 supplies the historical sound clue in 狹; Japanese readings can differ.
This 王 form represents 玉, jade, and supplies the meaning in 珠.
朱 supplies the sound element in 珠; Japanese readings depend on the word.

value.highlightedComponentText: The strokes below 心 were added later. They are separate from the heart and sound elements in the earlier form.
value.text: Earlier forms combined 心, heart, with a sound element written 旡. The upper shape changed over time; 心 remains recognizable.
The older round sun picture has a mark in its center. 日 keeps that central mark inside a squared outline.
月 began as a crescent-moon picture. Similar 月-shaped parts in other kanji can represent other things, such as 肉, flesh.
The older form pictures an eye. The modern 目 writes that eye upright.
Older forms show a bird with a head, body and hanging tail.
The older form pictures a horse with a head, mane and legs. The bottom dots in 馬 developed from legs; they do not mean fire here.
The older form pictures flowing water. Its central flowing line and side marks help you remember 水.
火 began as a picture of fire, with strokes spreading upward like flames.
本 adds a stroke near the base of 木, tree, to mark its roots.
A picture of a standing person seen from the side.
A picture of a person seen from the front.
The outline represents an open mouth.
A picture of an ear.
A picture of a hand and fingers.
An early picture of a leg.
The flowing lines represent a river.

value.compactText: Named the Han River in China.
value.text: 氵 marks water: 漢 first appears in early Western Zhou bronze inscriptions as a river name. The later use of 漢 for the Chinese people is linked to the prestige of the Han dynasty.
A picture of a field divided into sections.
The dots represent rain falling from a cloud.
An early picture of a mound of earth.
Two bamboo stalks with leaves.
A picture of rice grains.
A picture of a bundle of silk thread.
A picture of a bull’s head with horns.
A picture of a ram’s head.
A picture of a dog seen from the side.
An early picture of a fish.
An early picture of a carriage seen from above, with wheels on either side.
An early picture of a boat.
A picture of a gate. 戶 represents a single door.
An early picture of a knife.
A picture of a bow.
An early picture of flesh. Its component form can resemble 月.
An early picture of a heart, now highly stylized.
A picture of a person standing on the ground.
An early picture of a tall building.
An early picture of a person with long hair.
A short mark above a longer line represents above.
A short mark below a longer line represents below.
One stroke represents one.
Two strokes represent two.
Three strokes represent three.
末 marks the top of 木, tree, with an extra stroke: the tip or end.
刃 adds a mark to 刀, knife, to identify the blade.
A Japanese-created character combining 火, fire, and 田, field.
A Japanese-created character: 人 means person, and 動 supplies the onyomi ドウ.
A Japanese-created character combining 辵, movement, and 入, enter.
The older form shows a foot stepping out of a cave.
好 combines 女 (woman) and 子 (child). Affection between mother and child is one proposed explanation; the original reason for combining these parts is uncertain.
男 joins 田 (field) and 力 (strength), linking its older meaning of man with physical work in a field.
The three 口-shaped boxes in 品 represent various objects together, rather than three mouths.
In 腕, arm, the 月-shaped part is 肉 (flesh), marking a body part. It is not the moon.
In 腹, belly, the 月-shaped part is 肉 (flesh), marking a body part. It is not the moon.
In 肺, lung, the 月-shaped part is 肉 (flesh), marking a body part. It is not the moon.
In 肌, skin, the 月-shaped part is 肉 (flesh), marking a body part. It is not the moon.
胃 began as a picture of a stomach with food inside. Its modern 田-shaped top is a changed shape, not a field; flesh was added below.

value.compactText: Small above large: a pointed shape.
value.text: 小 small above 大 large outlines a shape that widens from its tip to its base.
炎 stacks two 火 fire shapes, one above the other.
The older form was a spiral representing rotation; the modern outline is squared.
A person 人 inside an enclosure 囗 represents a prisoner.

value.compactText: A dog and a mouth: barking.
value.text: 口 mouth combines with 犬 dog to express barking.

value.compactText: A bird and a mouth: calling.
value.text: 口 mouth combines with 鳥 bird for a bird's cry.
初 combines 衤 clothing and 刀 knife: cutting cloth begins making clothes.

value.compactText: An ear and a hand: taking.
value.text: 耳 ear and 又 hand show taking an ear.
分 combines 八, separating, with 刀, a knife: to divide.

value.compactText: Changed 大 and 火 shapes.
value.reviewNote: The source accounts interpret 大 as a person or as large. The lesson names the earlier shape without selecting its disputed contribution.
value.text: 赤 combines the older 大 and 火 shapes, linking the form to fire and red. Both parts later changed shape.

value.compactText: A running person above a foot.
value.text: 走 began with a running person; a foot was added below. Its 土-shaped top is a changed person shape.
止 began as a footprint with three toes and a sole.

value.compactText: Two people standing side by side.
value.text: 並 developed from 竝, which depicted two people standing side by side.

value.reviewNote: The held object is a stone axe in Wiktionary, but is explicitly unclear in verified Dong. Only the hand holding an object is admitted without qualification.
value.text: The older form pictures a hand holding an object, possibly a rod or axe.

value.compactText: 女 woman, marked with two dots.
value.text: 母 differentiates the older 女 woman shape with distinguishing dots.

value.compactText: A person with an open mouth.
value.text: The older form pictures a kneeling person with an open mouth.
The older shape is a vertical eye looking downward. It acquired the meanings servant and minister.
自 began as a nose picture and was later borrowed for the word self.

value.compactText: A face with a large eye.
value.text: 面 began as a face with an emphasized eye. The top horizontal stroke was added later.

value.compactText: 自 is the older nose shape.
value.text: The top 自 preserves the older nose shape; its use for self came later.
見 shows an eye above a person. Historical sources identify the older person shape differently.
禾 began as a picture of a plant stalk, more recognizable in older forms.
衣 began as the outline of the chest and upper clothing.

value.reviewNote: The sources agree on a ritual context but identify the object differently. The lesson does not select an altar or a memorial tablet as established fact.
value.text: 示 pictures a ritual object, interpreted as an altar or memorial tablet.
冊 pictures bamboo slips strung together.

value.compactText: A deer with changed leg shapes.
value.text: The deer picture changed over time: its legs became the modern 比-shaped base.
豕 began as a picture of a pig.
豚 combines 肉 flesh, written as the 月-shaped left part, with 豕 pig.

value.compactText: An elephant: trunk, head and body.
value.text: 象 began as an elephant picture. The upper ⺈-shaped part represents its trunk; the lower shapes represent its head and body.
The older tiger picture lost its torso; its legs and tail changed into the lower 儿-shaped part. The upper 虍 is the head.
爪 depicts a human hand grabbing from above; it can also indicate a claw.
角 began as a picture of a horn.
羽 pictures wings or feathers, shown as paired shapes.
矢 began as an arrow picture, clearer in older forms.

value.compactText: An earthenware jar with a lid.
value.text: 缶 began as an earthenware jar with a lid.
皿 began as a picture of an empty container; its handles joined in the modern shape.

value.compactText: The dot distinguishes 玉 from 王.
value.text: 玉 and 王 once had very similar shapes. A distinguishing dot separates 玉, jade, from 王, king.

value.compactText: A blood drop and a vessel.
value.text: 血 combines a blood-drop mark with 皿, a container.
串 pictures objects strung together, like pieces on a skewer.
The older form pictures a woman with folded arms. Its orientation and arm shapes changed in the modern character.

value.compactText: A baby with a large head and open arms.
value.text: The older picture shows a baby with a large head, spread arms and wrapped legs.
交 pictures a person with crossed legs. The upper body now resembles 立.
The older form of 京 pictures a tall building.
The older picture shows a kneeling woman breastfeeding a child; the woman resembles 母.

value.compactText: A person with the head emphasized.
value.text: 元 pictures a person with two strokes emphasizing the head, one attached to the body and one above.
果 began as a picture of fruit growing on a tree.
The older form of 毛 pictures hair or a feather.

value.compactText: The outline of a pregnant woman.
value.text: The older form of 身 pictures a pregnant woman.

value.compactText: A hand removing skin or fur.
value.text: The older form pictures a hand removing an animal's skin or fur.
The older form pictures a stretched animal hide, with its head above and tail and legs below.
The older form pictures a street intersection. Modern 行 writes its two sides as 彳 and 亍; it was originally one picture.
The older form of 飛 pictures a bird flying upward.
能 began as a bear picture. The two 匕-shaped parts represent paws, and the 月-shaped part developed from its face and open mouth.
The older form of 夕 pictures a crescent moon. It is a historical variant of 月.

value.compactText: A small island in a river.
value.text: The older form of 州 pictures a small island in a river.
The older form pictures a person wearing a headdress of feathers or ram's horns. That headdress is now written as 羊.
The older form of 巾 pictures a hanging piece of cloth.
桑 began as a mulberry-tree picture; its foliage became the modern 叒-shaped top.
The older form of 栗 pictures chestnuts growing on a tree.
The older form of 享 pictures an ancestral shrine.

value.compactText: A person wearing a ceremonial hat.
value.text: The older form pictures a person wearing a ceremonial hat.
The older form of 士 pictures a war axe.
The early form pictures a person with the buttocks emphasized. The later written form combines a body component with the historical sound component 九.
The early form pictures a person urinating. Its later written form combines a body-shaped part with water.
The older form pictures a swollen bud or sprout beginning to emerge.
己 may picture a silk rope used to bind things. It is distinct from 已 and 巳.

value.compactText: A spear handle wrapped with a strap.
value.text: The older form pictures a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap.
The older form pictures a ladle or dipper used to measure grain, held in a hand.
The older form of 才 pictures a sharp peg.
未 pictures a tree with additional or lush branches.
The older form pictures a dipper, comparable to 斗.
The older form pictures a pestle. It has a different origin from the similar-looking 干.
The older form of 又 pictures a right hand.
必 probably pictures a weapon handle with two decorative strokes. It did not develop from 心.
The older form pictures a three-pronged weapon or tool.

value.compactText: A bag tied at both ends.
value.text: The older form pictures a full bag tied at both ends. The sun-and-tree interpretation does not match the early shape.
The older form of 求 pictures a centipede.
The older form pictures a person dancing with objects held in both hands.

value.compactText: A wine vessel held in a hand.
value.text: The older form pictures a vessel held in a hand. The hand became the modern 寸-shaped part.
The older form pictures a ritual axe, a symbol of royal power. It has a different origin from 玉, jade.
The older form pictures fired pottery or a tile.
The older form of 申 pictures a lightning bolt.
The older form of 盾 pictures a shield.
石 began as a picture of a stone chime; the 口-shaped part was added later as decoration.
The older form pictures a mortar, the bowl used with a pestle.
The older form pictures a snake. 虫 was later used for insects as well.
The older form pictures a raincoat woven from plant fibers.
The older form of 豆 pictures a container.
The older form pictures a head. Its upper strokes developed from a hair-like shape.
The older form pictures a fish's spine. 肉, flesh, was added later, and the upper part changed into the modern shape.
The top began as a shoulder picture; the lower 月-shaped part represents flesh.

value.compactText: Flowers above a stalk and leaves.
value.text: The early form shows flowers above a plant's stalk and leaves. A plant component was added at the top later.

value.compactText: 卜 divination above a changed cauldron shape.
value.text: 貞 developed from a picture of a tripod cauldron, with 卜 later added for divination. The lower part changed into the modern 貝 shape.

value.compactText: A hand giving something to a person.
value.text: 付 combines a person with a hand, expressing giving or delivering something to someone.
企 combines a person and a foot, representing a person standing on tiptoes.
利 combines grain and a knife, expressing reaping grain.

value.compactText: A building and a hand: guarding.
value.text: 守 combines a building's roof with a hand to express guarding or defending a place. The hand element may also have supplied sound.
Both 尸 and the 匕-shaped part represent people in this character.

value.compactText: A person holding something on their head.
value.text: The oracle-bone form pictures a person holding something on their head with both hands. The later form also acquired a sound element.
料 combines rice with a dipper, expressing measuring or gauging.

value.compactText: Sweet and tree: a plum tree.
value.text: 某 combines 甘, sweet, with 木, tree; it originally wrote the plum tree.
登 combines two feet with a raised object or stepping stone. Some earlier forms also had two hands below.
相 combines an eye with a tree, expressing looking at a tree.
苗 combines grass with a field.

value.compactText: A knife separating a horn from a cow.
value.text: 解 combines a horn, a knife and a cow: a knife separating the horn from the animal.
隻 combines a bird and a hand, expressing holding one bird.
集 combines a bird and a tree.

value.compactText: A head with a beard or whiskers.
value.text: 須 began as a single picture of a head with hair at its side: a beard or whiskers. The picture later became more abstract.

value.compactText: A drum and a hand holding a drumstick.
value.text: 鼓 combines a drum with a hand holding a drumstick.
辻 was created in Japan for a crossroads. 辶 gives the idea of a road, and 十 shows two paths crossing.
躾 combines 身 (body) and 美 (beauty) in a Japanese-created character for discipline or upbringing.

value.compactText: 國 → 国: the enclosure stays; 玉 replaces 或.
value.text: 國 became 国: the enclosure stayed, while 或 changed to 玉. Here 玉 is a spelling change, not a clue about jade.

value.compactText: 國 → 国: the enclosure stays; 玉 replaces 或.
value.text: 國 became 国: the enclosure stayed, while 或 changed to 玉. Here 玉 is a spelling change, not a clue about jade.

value.conflict: The pinned Wiktionary account describes wings facing opposite directions; the human-verified Dong account describes people facing opposite directions. The pictured subject is disputed, so no whole-character picture or historical role is admitted.

Wiktionary presents a hand suppressing a kneeling person; human-verified Dong analyzes a hand meaning component and an 印 sound component with an earlier-form relationship. Their applicability to the modern written parts remains unresolved; roles and a whole-character lesson are withheld.

Wiktionary describes the pictured bend as a wrist or forearm, while human-verified Dong describes an elbow; both sources give elbow as the earlier meaning. No specific joint depiction is admitted pending review.

Wiktionary identifies the older picture as eggs or spawn, while human-verified Dong identifies a scrotum and treats egg as a later meaning. The pictured subject is disputed; no whole-character picture is admitted.

components.explanation: 糸 pictures thread; the upper shape's origin is disputed.
components.label: thread

value.conflict: Wiktionary identifies the upper shape as hands braiding thread, while human-verified Dong identifies raw silk hanging from a rack. The thread connection is supported, but the upper shape and whole picture are unresolved.
Wiktionary identifies the surrounding strokes as mountain walls, while human-verified Dong identifies mountain streams around an opening. No specific landscape picture or stroke identity is admitted.

The pinned sources disagree about the 口-shaped part: Wiktionary calls it a mouth, while human-verified Dong identifies a hole used in divination. The 卜 divination element is supported independently; the lower part retains neutral structure.

Wiktionary preserves both abbreviated 肘 as phonetic with 言 semantic and the Shuowen account of speech plus hand. 言 retains its meaning role; the modern 寸 occurrence remains neutral because its historical identity and function differ between these accounts.

Wiktionary assigns meaning to 行 and sound to 金. Unverified Dong assigns the opposite roles; it is not verified corroboration. Both visible occurrences remain neutral pending review of the competing accounts.

Wiktionary assigns sound to 𠩺 and meaning to 里. Human-verified Dong, attributed to CUHK without a dong tag, assigns sound to 里 and both sound and meaning to 𠩺. Retain the shared sound role of 𠩺 only; 里 remains neutral.
